lines.en: It is estimated that dozens of species disappear every day before scientists even discover them.
What makes the desert so remarkable is the variety of life that survives in such harsh conditions.
Not until the reserve was established did the number of gazelles begin to recover.
However small an island may be, it can hold species found nowhere else on Earth.
The migration is said to cover over ten thousand kilometers every single year.
Were the coral reefs to die, a quarter of all ocean life would lose its home.
It is not the strongest species that survives, but the one most able to adapt.
Little do we realize how deeply every creature is connected to the balance of its environment.
What conservation needs most is not more money, but more people who genuinely care.
Rarely does one person change the fate of a species, but every effort counts.
What scientists find most worrying is not extinction itself, but the speed at which it is accelerating.
It is through protecting small habitats that whole ecosystems can be saved.
Not until the hunting ban was strictly enforced did the eagle population start to rise again.
Were the mangrove forests to disappear, the coastline would lose its natural defense against storms.
It is the tiniest creatures, not the largest, that do the heaviest work in any ecosystem.
